newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is likely to visit Spain from May 18 to May 21.
Different human rights groups condemned Monday's evcition of some 300 prostitutes from a brothel in Dhaka by local people.
Bangladesh and Burmese authorities on Tuesday discussed the ways to resume the repatriation of Burmese Rohingya refugees.
Indian Border Security Forces on Sunday shot dead a Bangladeshi in a bordering village of southwestern Kushtia district.
Energy Minister Noor Uddin Khan on Tuesday said the government had no plan to import electricity from India at the moment but a set of conditions were now under consideration.
Asian Development Bank (ADB) said it would provide assistance to Bangladesh for development of its capital market.

The government will consider a proposal for a minimum wage of Tk 2,000 for garment workers after the formation of wage commission, State Minister for Labour and Manpower M A Mannan told the parliament on Tuesday.
The state-run Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC) suffered a loss of 4.95 billion taka because of subsidised sale of fertiliser during the current fiscal year (1996-97). REUTER
